text:
Tonight the moon dreams more lazily,

As if she were a beauty sunk among cushions

Who with discreet and very light hand caresses,

Before falling asleep, the contour of her breast.


On the silk back of sliding clouds,

Dying, she gives herself to prolonged ecstasies,

And lets her gaze wander over white visions

That rise into the blue like flowerings.


When upon this globe, with idle languor,

She lets a furtive tear roll down,

A pious poet, enemy of sleep,


Catches the cold drop in the hollow of his hand

like a fragment of opal with iridescent reflections.

And keeps it in his breast, far from the voracious sun.

translation.title: Sorrows of the Moon
translation.editorial_note: The translation keeps the moon's languid body, opal tear, and the sleepless poet preserving it from the sun.
